subject: Irregular chunk intervals causing WebSocket timeouts — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@gramline.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: ops@gramline.ai, priya@gramline.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:47:12 -0700
Subject: Realtime failures — intermittent WS silence and client-side timeouts

Hi Marcus,

We started seeing an increase in WebSocket disconnects and client-side timeouts on our production integration around 07:30 PDT this morning. Symptoms: long gaps (10-30s) between chunks, then either a forced reconnect or a 504 from our gateway. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~7% over the last hour and throughput dropped ~25%.

We pulled the capture and attached logs — you can see multiple requests where the final chunk never arrives and the client gives up. This is impacting user-facing features (live collaboration) so we need urgent help.

What we need from Redwood:
- Immediate triage and confirmation whether this is a platform regression or a customer-side issue
- If platform, an ETA for mitigation/fallback (canary to older runtime, routing, etc.)
- Any recommended short-term config we can use to reduce client timeouts

Attaching: redwood-run-logs-2027-05-03.txt, ws-capture-2027-05-03.pcap

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Director of Engineering, Gramline
--

Subject: Re: Realtime failures — intermittent WS silence and client-side timeouts

Folks — quick initial findings from the capture and logs (short version):

Observations:
- Several streams show irregular chunk emission intervals that correlate with increased loop latency in the low-priority batching queue. Normal chunk cadence ~200-400ms; affected requests show bursts with 4–18s gaps.
- KV cache hits and model backend RTT are normal. No obvious memory pressure on the serving hosts in the first pass.
- Pattern appears at roughly 07:28–07:45 across multiple pods in us-west-2 in the dedicated pool handling Gramline traffic.

Hypothesis:
- A scheduling regression in the batching worker introduced a priority inversion under medium burst load, causing long pauses in the chunk flush path. This matches commit range we rolled last night (kernel selection and a batching micro-optimization).

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back batching micro-optimization on one canary pool and are re-running captured requests — initial canary shows chunk cadence restored to <500ms.
- Increased batch flush frequency on the affected hosts as a temporary mitigation (pushing config via feature flags).
- Opened JIRA INC-9123 to track the root cause and roll forward/rollback plan.

Next steps:
- If canary holds for 15m, promote rollback to all dedicated hosts serving Gramline and flip fallback routing to that pool.
- Provide Gramline with a suggested client timeout and a short configuration snippet.

Attaching: links to canary logs in shared drive (see thread related_links).

—Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Escalation update — canary rollback completed, routing switch scheduled

Alex / Priya —

Quick executive summary:
- Root cause: batching worker priority inversion introduced in last-night micro-optimization; caused irregular chunk intervals and client timeouts in a subset of dedicated pool pods. (JIRA INC-9123)
- Mitigation completed: canary rollback to previous batching code promoted across Gramline-dedicated pool at 15:40 PDT today.
- Result: observed chunk cadence restored to ~250–500ms and error rate dropped back to baseline within 10 minutes of promotion. Throughput recovered to expected levels.

Immediate customer-facing changes we deployed:
- Promoted rollback across all dedicated hosts serving Gramline (15:40 PDT)
- Switched Gramline routing to the recovered pool and configured automatic fallback disabled while we validate stability
- Opened a postmortem working doc and scheduled a cross-functional RCA call tomorrow at 11:00 PDT (invites sent)

Attachments: redwood-run-logs-2027-05-03.txt, ws-capture-2027-05-03.pcap (for your records).

Next actions for Redwood (owners):
- Dev: complete root cause fix and regression tests (dev_patel)
- SE: coordinate with Gramline to validate client-side timeout recommendations and ingestion patterns (monica_patel)
- Ops: monitor the recovered pool for 24h and report any anomalies (laura_bennett)

Thanks again for the patience — please escalate to your execs if they need a one-page summary. I'll follow up after the RCA.

—Marcus Lin
